Topic T1 · First Impression

Where You'd Find It
The VMI bin card this module is named after — Item C1 sits in column C, row 1, highlighted in green.
The part itself, three views: the rounded dome, the threaded opening underneath, and the hex body.

What You’d Notice Picking This Up Cold

Item C1 is a small stainless nut that looks nothing like a standard hex nut: one end is closed off with a smooth, rounded dome.

Side view: the rounded dome sits on top of a six-sided (hex) body that a wrench grips.
The same shape as a standard drawing — side view and end view, with each dimension labelled by letter.

Domed Cap

The rounded, closed end is the whole point of the part — it covers the end of the bolt that passes through it.

Hex Body

Six flat sides let a wrench or socket turn the nut. Their width is the “width across flats” (see ).

Plain Stainless Finish

No coating or plating — just the bare silver surface of the stainless steel (see ).

Internal Thread

Hidden inside: an M6 coarse thread that mates with the bolt (see ).

Topic T3 · Standard & Nut Type

DIN 986 Domed Cap Nuts

The “MDL” in .6CMDLS points to one standard: DIN 986, which covers hexagon domed cap nuts.

Standard vs. Spec Sheet
DIN 986, page 1 — the title reads “Prevailing torque type, hexagon domed cap nuts, with nonmetallic insert.” It gives a reference drawing and the letters used for each dimension and tolerance. Read the full DIN 986 standard ↗

What Makes It an Acorn Nut
The standard’s drawing: the rounded top is the feature that defines this nut type.
The real part: a rounded (oval) dome on a hex body.

Acorn Nuts

Acorn nuts — also called cap nuts, crown nuts or dome nuts — have a rounded dome on one side. That single feature puts this part in the acorn-nut category.

The dome closes off one end, so the nut covers the threaded end of the bolt instead of leaving it exposed.

Topic T4 · Material Selection

18-8 (A2) Stainless Steel

The “S” at the end of .6CMDLS calls out the base material. Here’s what that grade actually means.

Requirement

Material: stainless steel, grade 18-8 (A2), strength class A2-70.

What “18-8” Means

The grade contains 18% chromium and 8% nickel — the two elements that give this stainless steel its character.

Stainless steel stock — 18-8 is a very common type, used in cookware, cutlery and many other applications.

Equivalent Grade

18-8 (A2) is also known as 304 stainless steel.

What “A2” Means

A2 is the steel grade: an austenitic steel. It cannot be hardened by heat treatment — only by cold working. Defined in ISO 3506-1:1997.

What “70” Means

The second block, A2-70, is the strength class: a minimum tensile strength of 700 N/mm² (700 MPa).

Marked on the Part

This material grade is marked on the part itself.

ISO 3506-1 Table 1 — stainless steel grades by chemical composition. The A2 row (austenitic group) is the one this part uses.

Topic T5 · Finish

Plain — No Finish

Some parts have a coating, plating or treatment added after they are made. This one doesn’t.

Requirement

None. This piece has no finish, so it remains plain.

In the Part Number

There is no finish suffix after the “S” — a plain part simply ends at the material code.

What You See

The natural surface of the stainless steel, with nothing applied on top.

The finished nuts: plain stainless steel, no coating.

Topic T6 · Thread & Gauging

M6-1.0 6H Internal Thread

The thread inside the dome is an M6 — here is what that means, and how SBS checks it.

The Thread on the Drawing
The drawing’s section view calls out the thread as M6-1.0 6H.

Thread Size

M6 — a metric thread with a 6 mm nominal diameter, matching the “6” in the part number.

Thread Pitch

1.0 mm — the distance from one thread crest to the next.

Verifying the Pitch with a Plug Gauge

Go / No-Go Plug Gauge

  1. Two ends, two jobs. A plug gauge has a GO end and a NO GO end.
  2. GO end: it must pass into the thread. If it does, the thread is correct.
  3. NO GO end: it must not pass into the thread.
  4. If the results differ from this, the piece must be rejected.
An M6x1-6H plug gauge: GO on one end, NO GO on the other.
Finding the Thread Type on the Chart
The thread pitch identification chart (the “Black Book” table), with the M6 row highlighted.

Coarse Thread

Looking up M6-1.0 on the Black Book thread reference table shows that it corresponds to a coarse thread — the “C” in .6CMDLS.

Topic T7 · Key Dimensions

Width Across Flats & Height

Two dimensions matter most when checking a domed cap nut by hand: how wide the hex is, and how tall the nut is.

Letter s on the drawing marks the width across flats.
Measured with a digital caliper: 9.85 mm.

Width Across Flats (s)

Minimum 9.78 mm, maximum 10.00 mm, identified by the letter s. Sample measured 9.85 mm — inside the range.

Where the numbers come from: DIN 986 Table 1, M6 column, s rows — nominal size 10 (max), min 9.78. Read the full DIN 986 standard ↗
Height (h2)
Letter and number h2 on the drawing marks the overall height.
Measured with a digital caliper: 12.27 mm.

Height (h₂)

Minimum 11.65 mm, maximum 12.35 mm, identified as h2. Sample measured 12.27 mm — inside the range.

Where the numbers come from: DIN 986 Table 1, M6 column, h2 rows — nominal 12, max 12.35, min 11.65. Read the full DIN 986 standard ↗

Topic T8 · Inspection & Quality

How SBS Checks the Part Against Print

Every lot of .6CMDLS is checked against an inspection report built from the DIN 986 standard and the item specification.

Visual & Document Checks

Burrs and thread aesthetic, material (S/S) and surface finish/color (plain) are confirmed by visual inspection or by documents.

Caliper Checks

Width across flats (s), width across corners (e) and height (h2) are measured with a caliper.

Plug Gage Check

The M6-1.0 6H thread is checked with a plug gage — pass or fail.

Print / Spec

The report cites DIN 986 as the print/spec, with the item description and extended description (stainless steel).

Inspection Template & Inspection Report
Click any document to enlarge.

Inspection Template

A blank form prepared by the Quality team that shows how to determine whether a part conforms. It is a controlled document, linked to the part in P21.

Inspection Report

When a lot is inspected, the dimensions and the evaluation of the part are recorded on a copy of the template. That copy is the Inspection Report, found in SBS Connect for review — for example after a customer complaint.

Click a number on the template to see exactly where that dimension and tolerance comes from in DIN 986.

1 · Width Across Flats – s

Min 9.78 / Max 10.00 (report row 4, caliper).
DIN 986 Table 1, M6 column, s rows: nominal size 10, min 9.78.

2 · Width Across Corners – e

Min 11.05 (report row 5, caliper).
DIN 986 Table 1, M6 column, e row: min 11.05.

3 · Height – h2

Min 11.65 / Max 12.35 (report row 6, caliper).
DIN 986 Table 1, M6 column, h2 rows: nominal 12, max 12.35, min 11.65.

4 · Thread

M6-1.0 6H, checked with a plug gage (pass/fail, report row 7).
DIN 986 Table 1 gives the M6 size and the P = 1 mm coarse pitch; the 6H tolerance class is called out on the print.

The template’s feature / tolerance table — the numbered pins match the DIN 986 table.
DIN 986, Table 1 (M6 column). Read the full DIN 986 standard ↗

Material, surface finish, burrs and thread aesthetic are checked against the print and item specification, not DIN 986.

Topic T9 · Applications

Where Domed Cap Nuts Are Used

Parts like this one turn up in many industries — and the dome does real work.

Industries
Domed cap nuts in the field (click to enlarge).

Industries That Use Them

Automotive, food and construction, among others.

What the Dome Does
  • Protects objects near the end of the bolt against scratches and structural damage.
  • Reduces accidents on human skin.
  • Gives the assembly a nice appearance with a smooth, finished look.
  • Covers threaded ends so they are not left exposed.

    Reference

    Glossary

    Every code, acronym, and standard used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term’s “jump” button to see it in context.

    18-8 (A2) Stainless Steel

    A common grade of stainless steel, also known as 304. “18-8” means 18% chromium and 8% nickel. “A2” is the grade in ISO 3506-1.

    A2-70

    The strength class of the stainless steel. The “70” indicates a minimum tensile strength of 700 N/mm² (700 MPa).

    Acorn Nut (Domed Cap Nut)

    A nut with a rounded dome closing one end, also called a cap nut, crown nut or dome nut. It covers the threaded end of the bolt.

    Austenitic

    The steel family A2 belongs to. It cannot be hardened by heat treatment, only by cold working.

    Coarse Thread

    The standard, larger thread pitch for a given diameter. For M6 this is 1.0 mm, and it is the “C” in the part number.

    DIN 986

    The German standard for prevailing-torque hexagon domed cap nuts with a non-metallic insert. It defines the dimensions and tolerances of this part.

    Go / No-Go Plug Gauge

    A two-ended gauge for checking an internal thread. The GO end must pass in and the NO GO end must not; otherwise the part is rejected.

    Inspection Template & Report

    The template is a controlled blank form showing how to judge whether a part conforms. A filled-in copy from an inspected lot is the Inspection Report.

    ISO 3506-1

    The international standard for mechanical properties of corrosion-resistant stainless steel fasteners, including the A2 grade.

    Plain (Finish)

    No coating, plating or treatment — the bare stainless steel surface.

    Thread Pitch

    The distance between neighbouring thread crests. M6-1.0 has a 1.0 mm pitch.

    VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory)

    A bin system where SBS manages and restocks parts directly at the customer’s location. This training module is named after Item C1’s cell on the VMI bin card.

    Width Across Flats (s)

    The distance between two opposite flat sides of the hex body. For this nut: 9.78 – 10.00 mm.
